claims.text: The unchanged (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field operation.
The unchanged alloy exhibits a large caloric response under pressure-field operation.
The unchanged alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and is prone to cracking.
A tailored heat treatment can induce a bimodal grain structure consisting of a fine-grained matrix and coarse grains in this alloy.
The tailored heat treatment can introduce or segregate nanoprecipitates at grain boundaries.
The resulting nanoprecipitate-reinforced grain boundaries will arrest crack propagation.
Refined grains will improve the alloy's toughness.
Refined grains will distribute mechanical stress more uniformly.
Grain-boundary nanoprecipitates will impede crack initiation.
Grain-boundary nanoprecipitates will impede crack growth.
The engineered microstructure can provide mechanical reinforcement without interfering with the phase transformations responsible for the caloric response.
Relative to the unchanged alloy, the heat-treated alloy will have increased load-bearing capacity.
Relative to the unchanged alloy, the heat-treated alloy will exhibit less cracking.
The heat-treated alloy will retain a large caloric effect under applied-field operation relative to the unchanged alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will retain a large caloric effect under pressure-field operation relative to the unchanged alloy.
Excessive heat-treatment temperature or duration could alter the caloric phase transformation.
The processing window needed to produce the desired microstructure without degrading the caloric phase is not presently specified.
